fields.oneLiner: DabbaRoute plans the morning delivery route for a home tiffin kitchen and sends each rider his stop list on WhatsApp.
fields.jobStory:
When a home tiffin kitchen takes on a new customer in the middle of the month, the owner has to re-plan the whole morning route in her head before 10:30am, so I can hand each rider a stop list that is actually in order and stop the 1pm calls asking where the dabba is.

Who has this job: single-kitchen tiffin operators in Pune doing 40 to 150 dabbas a day, the ones running out of a flat in Kothrud, Karve Nagar and Warje who advertise on society WhatsApp groups and hostel notice boards. I met eleven of them by walking into kitchens between 3 and 5pm, which is the only hour they are free. Nine were women over 40 running the kitchen with one or two riders on their own bikes.

What they do instead: the route lives in the owner's head or on a torn notebook page, and it gets re-sorted by shouting at the rider while he is already on the bike. Two of the eleven had tried Google Maps with pins and gave up, because re-ordering sixty pins on a phone before lunch is not happening. One pays 3,000 rupees a month to a nephew to rebuild a Google Sheet every Sunday, which breaks the moment somebody cancels on a Tuesday.
fields.trafficTestNotes:
Three sources over eleven days, 24 August to 3 September 2026.

1. Facebook group 'Pune Tiffin and Catering Suppliers', 18k members. Two posts, 26 Aug and 1 Sep, each with a photo of a printed stop list. Group insights showed 2,340 and 1,880 reach. 104 clicks through to the tally form, 22 signups.

2. Meta ads, 1,400 rupees over five days, 28 Aug to 1 Sep. Radius of 25km around Pune, interest set to catering and food business, creative in Marathi and Hindi. 11,420 impressions, 157 clicks (1.37% CTR), 12 signups. That is about 116 rupees per signup.

3. Door to door. I walked into 14 kitchens in Kothrud and Karve Nagar with a one page printout and a QR code. 7 scanned it, 7 signed up. I am counting this separately because I was standing in the room, which is not the same as cold traffic.

Spend: 1,400 on ads plus 180 on printing. The tally dashboard is the source of truth for both numbers: 268 views of the form against 41 responses, which it reports as 15.3%. That is high. It is high because two of the three sources are people who already run tiffin kitchens rather than a general audience. The Meta ads on their own convert at 7.6% (12 of 157) and I think that is the honest number to plan with.

The last signup came in on the evening of 3 September, which is where I stopped and took the screenshot.

notes: Every clause is answered with something checkable: a narrow audience the student physically visited, a named alternative, three named traffic sources with reach, visits and spend, and a screenshot whose 41 responses, 268 views and 3 September date all match what was reported. The high conversion is explained rather than boasted about.
